newsitem.title: CHINA: Death toll in China mine accidents up 2.89 percent.
newsitem.headline: Death toll in China mine accidents up 2.89 percent.

text.p: Deaths as a result of accidents at mines in China rose by 2.89 percent in the first 10 months of this year although casualties from fires and train accidents declined, the Workers Daily said on Friday.

Casualties from road accidents also rose, with the number of accidents rising by 5.6 percent, deaths up by 3.9 percent and injuries up by 9.0 percent compared with January-October 1995, the newspaper quoted Vice-Premier Wu Bangguo as saying.
In the first 10 months of this year, the number of deaths from mining accidents rose by 2.89 percent compared with the year-ago period, Wu said. He gave no figures.
The number of fires, fatal rail accidents and non-mining industry accidents fell in the first 10 months, Wu said.
An official of the Ministry of Labour declined to give the exact number of deaths in mining accidents, saying the figure was a state secret.
However, government statistics show that mine explosions, collapses and other accidents kill up to 10,000 miners a year in China.
